lines: Robert Scott risked his own life to rescue dogs from a crevasse.
Yet Scott doubted that dogs were reliable.
On his Discovery expedition, his dogs died of disease.
So Scott bet on motor sledges instead.
But in 1909, he realised motors were unlikely to get him to the Pole.
So he also took ponies, dogs and skis.
His ship carried 34 dogs, 19 Siberian ponies and three motor sledges.
One motor sledge broke through the sea ice and sank.
You see, dogs were like a new bike: wonderful in the right hands, useless in the wrong ones.
Slowly, Scott grew more impressed with the dogs.
By 1 November, both motor sledges had failed.
His men hauled 740 pounds of supplies by hand.
So Scott ordered the dog teams to meet him on the way home, on 1 March.
Scott reached the meeting point three days early.
A blizzard stopped him 11 miles south of One Ton Depot.
In 2012, Scott's written orders for the dogs were re-discovered.
The man who once doubted dogs had counted on them to bring him home.

claims.claim: Scott returned to Safety Camp with the dogs, after risking his own life to rescue a dog-team that had fallen into a crevasse, on the depot-laying journey.
Scott's experiences on Discovery had made him dubious of the reliability of dogs; on Discovery the dogs succumbed to disease in the first season.
Scott thought he could resolve the motor traction problem by developing a tracked snow motor.
In the middle of 1909, Scott realised that motors were unlikely to get him all the way to the Pole and decided additionally to take horses, dogs and skis.
Terra Nova took aboard 34 dogs, 19 Siberian ponies and three motorised sledges.
One of the motor sledges was lost during unloading, breaking through the sea ice and sinking.
Scott recognised the dogs' effectiveness in the right hands and became increasingly impressed with their capabilities.
By 1 November both motor sledges had failed, and the party man-hauled 740 pounds of supplies.
Scott ordered that the dog teams meet the polar party between latitude 82 and 82.30 on 1 March to assist the party home.
Scott reached the meeting point for the dog teams three days ahead of schedule; the dog teams did not appear.
Scott, Wilson and Bowers struggled on to a point 11 miles south of One Ton Depot, but were halted by a fierce blizzard.
In 2012, Karen May at the Scott Polar Research Institute re-discovered Scott's written orders for the dog teams.

cast.scott: a 42 year old English naval officer explorer, sturdy build, a broad clean-shaven wind-burnt face with a strong jaw, short thinning brown hair, steady grey eyes, wearing a pale khaki windproof smock over a thick cream wool sweater and a dark blue naval peaked cap, 1910s
cast.meares: a 33 year old British dog driver, wiry build, a narrow tanned face, a thin black moustache, black hair under a rolled grey knitted balaclava, wearing a dark green wool anorak with a leather belt and sealskin mittens, 1910s
cast.researcher: a 50 year old woman archivist with a short straight silver-white bob, black rectangular reading glasses, a navy blue wool jumper with a white collar, 2010s
